headline: Rate spike and Iran-linked oil surge sour risk appetite
body: Treasuries did most of the talking this week: the 10-year yield spiked to roughly 5.11% on Wednesday, its highest since 2007, in one of the sharpest single-day jumps in nearly a year and a half, while the 5-year note briefly touched 5% for the first time since 2007 too. The move was driven by stronger-than-expected manufacturing survey data, hawkish commentary from a Fed official, and a poorly received five-year auction — a combination that reads as 'the economy is fine, but rate relief isn't coming as fast as hoped.' Equities took the hit directly: the S&P 500 fell 0.75%, the Nasdaq dropped 1.13% and small-caps underperformed further, the signature of a rate-driven de-risking rather than a growth scare. Futures stayed pressured into Thursday, extending the cautious tone.

Oil is compounding the story. Brent has been volatile around the $100 mark as the U.S.-Iran standoff drags on, with traders parsing dueling rhetoric at the UN General Assembly for signs of escalation or de-escalation; energy-sensitive names like airlines and cruise operators slipped in premarket trading on the renewed inflation-via-crude worry. Markets are also bracing for a closely watched Trump-Xi summit this week, with AI policy reportedly high on the agenda — another source of headline risk rather than resolution. Retail chatter stayed thin on anything beyond the usual index-option and mega-cap-tech mentions, so today's read leans far more on rates and geopolitics than on any organized shift in social sentiment.
